parsed.population_and_sample: 16 different civil society-state partnerships, 24 participants (representatives of CSOs, local government District Assemblies, and donors) in the Northern region of Ghana
parsed.exposure: State-civil society partnerships (project, network, and strategic collaborations) within the context of decentralization policies and public sector reforms
parsed.outcome: Improved access to safe water and sanitation coverage, and service sustainability
parsed.rationale: The study investigates state-civil society partnerships and their impact on water and sanitation service coverage in Ghana, satisfying all inclusion criteria. It uses an exploratory qualitative design with empirical evidence from 24 in-depth interviews across 16 partnership cases. As detailed in the Abstract and Section 4, the findings provide empirical insights into the drivers, nature, and challenges of these collaborations in improving service access for marginalized communities.
